Caffeine can enhance athletic performance primarily by increasing alertness and reducing perceived effort. Many athletes use it before endurance workouts (running, cycling, rowing) or high-intensity interval sessions where focus and tolerance for discomfort matter.

A practical approach is to start with a low dose in training (not on race day) to assess tolerance. Commonly used amounts are around 1–3 mg/kg taken 30–60 minutes before exercise, but sensitivity varies widely. If you experience jitters, rapid heartbeat, stomach upset, or anxiety, reduce the dose or avoid it.

To make results reproducible, keep variables consistent: use the same caffeine source (coffee, tea, tablet), take it at the same pre-exercise time window, and compare similar workouts. Also consider sleep—late-day caffeine can impair rest, which can hurt performance more than caffeine helps.
